title: SafeWindow
tagline: When does each village lose its last road to a flood shelter?
supply_help: Days of food and water a family has on hand once cut off. This is an assumption, not a measurement.
showing: Map shows the flood observed on {d} ({src}).
no_obs: No observation on or before this date - showing the first one ({d}).
unknown_note: {p}% of the area had no radar observation that day (outside the satellite's path) - shown in grey.
uncertain: uncertain (roads not covered by radar that day)
seen_detail: Connected on all {c} dates its roads were observed. On the other {u} dates the radar did not cover its roads.
uncertain_note: Its roads were not observed on some dates, so its status on those dates is unknown. Treat dates as ranges, not certainties.
source_caption: Built from public satellite data by the SafeWindow pipeline. Not an official warning system.
roads_note: Model route status at cut thresholds 10% / 20% / 40%, on the last radar view before and the first after each reported date.
how_text: A village counts as isolated only when no road route to any shelter is left. The isolation range runs from the day after it was last seen connected to the day it was first seen isolated. The safe exit date is the last day it was seen connected. The aid deadline adds the supply days chosen on the left to the earliest possible isolation day.
pick: Select a village (or click one on the map)
never: Not isolated on any observed date
no_exit: No safe exit observed (already cut off on the first image)
modis: Flooded area seen by NASA MODIS (MOD09GA proxy; monsoon cloud hides most of the area)
limits_text:
- Supply days is an assumption, not measured.
- Flood maps have gaps where the radar did not pass, and radar errors; dates between images are ranges.
- OpenStreetMap roads are incomplete, and the shelters are unverified OpenStreetMap candidates (schools, clinics, offices).
- Research prototype, not an official warning system. Follow official alerts ({agencies}).
bag_items: ID papers and money in a waterproof bag
Charged phone, power bank and a torch
contacts_none: Ask your local disaster-management office or community leaders for the emergency number.
card_tip_list: Leave before the last safe exit date on this card; do not wait for water to reach the house.
Go in a group and tell a neighbour which route you are taking.
Never walk or drive through moving flood water.
If you cannot reach the shelter, go to the highest dry building and stay there.
An SMS often goes through when calls do not. Send the message below to family or the local office.
Switch the phone to low-power mode and keep calls short.
card_disclaimer: Provisional estimate from satellite data. Not an official warning. Shelters are unverified. Follow official alerts ({agencies}) and local officials first.
pack_howto: Save this file on your phone now. It opens with no internet and no app: use any browser, search your village and read your card. Print it if you can.
card_made: Made on {d} from satellite data seen on {o}. Supply assumption: {n} days.
status_isolated: Cut off from every shelter by road
status_ok: Roads to a shelter were open on every date observed
status_unknown: Road status uncertain: some dates have no radar view
go_none: No safe road route was observed. Move to the highest dry building, stay together, and send the SMS below.
go_ok: Roads to a shelter were open. Keep this card and leave early if water rises.
walk: About {h} hours on foot on dry road (estimate; slower in water or at night).
offline_title: No internet? Save for offline use
dl_pack: Download the offline pack for all villages
offline_help: The app needs a network. Download the pack before the flood or when the network returns: it opens with no internet on any phone or PC and prints one page per village.
lowdata_help: Shows villages, shelters and routes without downloading map tiles. Use on a weak connection.

help_btn: Write an SMS with my village and location
help_note: Opens your messages app with the text filled in. Choose the number of your local office or a relative, then send. An SMS often goes through when calls fail.
help_body: HELP. Village: {name}. People: {p}. Location: {loc}. Sent from a SafeWindow card.
draft_notice: Draft translation: not yet checked by a native speaker. Confirm anything important with local officials.
contacts_112: International emergency number (a standard on most mobile networks; confirm your local number)
overview_help: Move the slider to replay the flood. Tap a village to open its card. Blue squares are shelter candidates (unverified).
health_line: {name}: about {km} km {dir} in a straight line, not a road route. Roads may be cut: call for help first.
stages_title: What to do: before, during and after a flood
stage_before: Charge phones and power banks, and fill containers with clean water.
Move documents, medicine and food to a high place, and pack the items on your card.
Agree a meeting point and route with your family, and know your last safe exit date.
Keep this pack saved on your phone, and switch off the electricity if water may enter the house.
stage_during: Leave early: do not wait for the water to reach the house.
Never walk, swim or drive through moving floodwater: it hides holes, wires and debris.
Stay away from electric wires and anything wet that is plugged in.
If you are trapped, go to the highest dry place and send the help SMS; keep the family together.
stage_after: Return only when officials say it is safe; avoid damaged buildings and floodwater.
Boil or treat all drinking water, and throw away food that touched floodwater.
Watch for diarrhoea, fever and skin infections; use ORS and seek care early.
Watch for snakes and other animals sheltering in dry places.
health_none: No hospital or clinic is listed for this area. Ask your local office, or call the emergency number, to find the nearest health post.
